strengths: Addresses a significant and challenging open problem in algorithmic mechanism design: designing budget-feasible mechanisms for submodular social welfare maximization with private costs.

Provides the first budget-feasible descending clock mechanism (BFM-SWM) achieving provable approximation guarantees (in the standard regularized sense $\gamma v(O) - c(O)$) for both general non-monotone (0.0328) and monotone (0.0877) submodular valuations, while guaranteeing truthfulness (obvious strategyproofness), individual rationality, budget feasibility, and non-negative auctioneer surplus.

Yields a valuable by-product mechanism (BFM-VM) for the classical submodular valuation maximization problem, substantially improving the best-known deterministic approximation ratio from 1/64 (~0.0156) by Balkanski et al. (SODA 2022) to 1/(12 + 4\sqrt{3}) (~0.0528) and reducing time complexity from O(n^2 log n) to O(n log n).

The theoretical framework is technically sound, combining progressive geometrically increasing thresholds, ownership routing across multiple candidate sequences, and protective singleton solutions to circumvent unobservable private costs.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation on real-world datasets (influence maximization on network graphs and crowdsourced image summarization on CIFAR-10) validating strong objective performance and superior query efficiency over existing methods.
weaknesses: Because prior welfare maximization mechanisms (e.g., Deng et al., 2025) do not enforce budget feasibility, the baselines in Section 6 are evaluated using an ad-hoc prefix-truncation heuristic; while justifiable given the absence of directly comparable prior work, this inherently puts the baselines at a disadvantage.

The running time and additive error of BFM-SWM depend on the scale of the optimal welfare and the parameter $\epsilon$ ($O(n \log(OPT / \epsilon))$), requiring at least a coarse estimate or lower bound on the optimal value scale to set $\epsilon$ appropriately in practice.
The paper would benefit from a deeper discussion on the theoretical limitations/barriers regarding lower bounds for deterministic or randomized budget-feasible welfare maximization.

strengths: Addresses a significant and challenging open problem: designing budget-feasible mechanisms for submodular welfare maximization in procurement auctions with private seller costs.

First provable approximation guarantees for this setting: achieves a 0.0328-approximation for general submodular valuation functions and a 0.0877-approximation for monotone valuations (up to an arbitrarily small additive error), while strictly satisfying obvious strategyproofness, individual rationality, budget feasibility, and non-negative auctioneer surplus.

Strong technical by-product for valuation maximization: the deterministic variant BFM-VM improves the state-of-the-art deterministic approximation ratio from 1/64 (~0.0156) by Balkanski et al. (SODA 2022) to 1/(12 + 4√3) (~0.0528), while reducing the time complexity from O(n^2 log n) to O(n log n).

Clear, well-crafted mechanism design: the interplay of the progressive geometric threshold, the dual candidate set sequences, and the break condition cleverly guarantees both budget feasibility and a non-negative buyer surplus without requiring direct oracle access to private costs.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation on both influence maximization and crowdsourced image summarization, demonstrating substantial empirical gains in both social welfare and valuation objectives along with major reductions in oracle query complexity.
weaknesses: The baseline comparison in Section 6 necessarily relies on a heuristic truncation of unconstrained mechanisms from Deng et al. (2025) because no native budget-feasible mechanisms for welfare maximization previously existed; while reasonable, this somewhat limits the competitiveness of the comparison baselines.

The theoretical multiplicative approximation constant for general submodular welfare maximization (0.0328) remains relatively modest, although this is common in non-monotone submodular budget-feasible mechanism design.
The runtime bound depends logarithmically on 1/ϵ, introducing an additive loss in the theoretical approximation guarantee.

strengths: First budget-feasible mechanism for welfare maximization: The paper addresses a significant and challenging open problem in algorithmic mechanism design by proposing BFM-SWM, the first budget-feasible mechanism with provable approximation guarantees for submodular welfare maximization (both general and monotone) under private seller costs.

Major theoretical improvement on deterministic valuation maximization: As a by-product, BFM-VM establishes a deterministic approximation ratio of 1/(12 + 4√3) ≈ 0.0528 for general submodular valuation maximization, substantially improving upon the best-known deterministic ratio of 1/64 ≈ 0.0156 by Balkanski et al. (SODA 2022), while also improving the runtime complexity from O(n^2 log n) to O(n log n).

Clean and sound technical framework: The algorithmic design—combining geometrically increasing thresholds, the value-to-payment parameter β to ensure budget feasibility and non-negative surplus, and singleton protection—is elegant and mathematically rigorous, yielding clean proofs across all settings.

Comprehensive empirical validation: The mechanisms are evaluated across multiple large-scale SNAP graphs for influence maximization and CIFAR-10 for crowdsourcing, assessing welfare, oracle query complexity, and wall-clock runtime against relevant baselines.
weaknesses: Nature of the welfare approximation guarantee: The approximation notion used, v(S) - c(S) ≥ γ_w · v(O) - c(O) - ε, while standard in regularized submodular maximization due to hardness results, can become uninformative or trivially satisfied when the optimal cost c(O) is close to γ_w · v(O). The paper would benefit from a more explicit discussion of the operational regime where this guarantee provides meaningful lower bounds.

Oversimplified discussion of obvious strategyproofness (OSP): In the proof of Theorem 4.1, the authors assert that OSP 'follows immediately from the observation that the mechanism takes the form of a descending clock auction.' While descending clock auctions often satisfy OSP, formal OSP requires verifying the earliest-divergence condition across the extensive-form game tree, which should be explicitly stated rather than asserted as immediate.

Baseline selection in empirical evaluation: The welfare maximization baselines are adapted from Deng et al. (2025) by truncating unconstrained solutions when the budget is reached. While understandable given that no prior budget-feasible welfare mechanisms exist, the evaluation would be strengthened by also comparing against budget-feasible valuation maximization mechanisms (e.g., Balkanski et al. 2022, Han et al. 2025) evaluated under the net welfare metric v(S) - c(S).

Relatively small constant factors: Although the theoretical guarantees are the first of their kind for budget-feasible welfare maximization, the approximation factors (0.0328 for general submodular and 0.0877 for monotone) remain quite small.
